title: Catalogue search, sorting and category filter

sourcesRead.contributes: description, catalogue API, acceptance criteria 1-7, notes

context: As a shopper I want to search, sort and filter the tool catalogue so that I find the right tool quickly. The web shop and the public catalogue API (used by the mobile app) must behave the same way.

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Searching the web shop for a term shows only products whose name contains the term, and a caption "Searched for: <term>".
acceptanceCriteria.text: Searching the web shop for a term shows only products whose name contains the term, and a caption "Searched for: <term>".
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop catalogue (route and search control: G1)
outcomes: every product shown has a name that contains the term

acceptanceCriteria.quote: GET /products/search?q=<term> returns 200 with only products whose name contains the term, regardless of letter case (searching "PLIERS" finds the same products as "pliers").
acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /products/search?q=<term> returns 200 with only products whose name contains the term, regardless of letter case (searching "PLIERS" finds the same products as "pliers").
outcomes: every product in data has a name that contains the term, regardless of letter case
searching "PLIERS" finds the same products as "pliers"

acceptanceCriteria.quote: A search without matches shows "There are no products found." on the web shop, and the API returns 200 with an empty data list and total 0.
acceptanceCriteria.text: A search without matches shows "There are no products found." on the web shop, and the API returns 200 with an empty data list and total 0.
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop catalogue (route and search control: G1)
outcomes: web shop shows "There are no products found."
API: data is an empty list

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Choosing "Price (Low - High)" on the web shop lists the products by ascending price; GET /products?sort=price,asc returns the products in ascending price order.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Choosing "Price (Low - High)" on the web shop lists the products by ascending price; GET /products?sort=price,asc returns the products in ascending price order.
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop catalogue (route and sort control: G1)
outcomes: web shop: after choosing "Price (Low - High)" the products are listed by ascending price
API: GET /products?sort=price,asc returns the products in ascending price order

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Filtering the web shop by the category "Hammer" shows only hammers; GET /products?by_category=<id of Hammer> returns only products in that category.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Filtering the web shop by the category "Hammer" shows only hammers; GET /products?by_category=<id of Hammer> returns only products in that category.
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop catalogue (route and category filter: G1)
outcomes: web shop: filtering by the category "Hammer" shows only hammers
API: GET /products?by_category=<id of Hammer> returns only products in the category "Hammer"

acceptanceCriteria.quote: Results are paginated with 12 products per page (per_page 12) on the web shop and in the API.
acceptanceCriteria.text: Results are paginated with 12 products per page (per_page 12) on the web shop and in the API.
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop catalogue (route and pagination: G1)
outcomes: web shop: results are paginated with 12 products per page

acceptanceCriteria.quote: An empty search (no term) returns all products, so the mobile app can reuse the search endpoint for its "All tools" screen.
acceptanceCriteria.text: An empty search (no term) returns all products, so the mobile app can reuse the search endpoint for its "All tools" screen.
outcomes: a search with no term returns all products

endpoints.request: list; query parameters sort (e.g. ?sort=price,asc) and by_category (?by_category=<category id>); paginated. Public catalogue API (story.md#L18)
source of category ids (e.g. the id of "Hammer" for by_category)

rules.text: The web shop and the public catalogue API (used by the mobile app) must behave the same way.
